data.summary: Landed: MAME INI isolation (main 23e78a9). Every automated MAME run takes one isolated argument set, so no mame.ini or user config leaks into a trace or recording
data.body: Four commits on f457e56, gated and Codex-approved. cec9d12 adds mame_args (xtask/src/sound.rs): the set, -rompath, -noreadconfig, -inipath <run dir>/ini, -video none, -sound none, -nothrottle, -window, a fixed -samplerate, and per-run cfg, nvram and snapshot directories. data.summary: Landed: per-game files and a decisions.md merge driver (main e9619af). Two branches editing the same decision now conflict instead of both surviving a union merge
data.body: Per-game files splits the shared docs (docs/mechanics/<game>.md and the like) so parallel game branches stop conflicting; game branches move over with `cargo xtask split-docs --branch --dir <worktree>`. docs/decisions.md merges through tools/merge-decisions: a normal three-way merge first; if that conflicts and both sides only added rows it keeps both (as union did, checked by line count); if either side changed or removed a row the conflict stays and parity refuses the markers. Each clone runs once: git config merge.decisions.driver "tools/merge-decisions %O %A %B %L %P" (AGENTS.md step 6). Without it git falls back to a normal text merge, so the worst case is an ordinary conflict. Worth copying if your decisions table is edited on parallel branches; the carry-over cell of our decisions row says so.

data.summary: VectorCraft landed land --queue --keep-going and an ssh-drop-proof Studio gate
data.body: Main 19a6ef7. (1) `cargo xtask land --queue --keep-going`: a branch that fails before landing is put back (reset only from the tip the queue made, old tip kept under refs/archive/), the rest land, and the run ends with a table, the retry command and a nonzero exit. Worth copying if you gate on the Studio: tools/gate-host + xtask/src/gate_host.rs, and the caffeinate block in .githooks/codex-review run with its test.sh check. data.body: Main 0fe56ea. data.summary: VectorCraft: Studio gates could build another tree's code and pass; fixed (lane before checkout, target-dir flock)
data.body: Main 2cce6f5. A Studio gate failed with code its tip didn't have. Cause: tools/gate-host checked out the run's worktree BEFORE waiting for its lane. While it waited, another gate built its own tree in that lane's target dir. Cargo's freshness check uses mtimes and package-relative paths, so every file older than that build counted as built, and the gate compiled the other tree's vc-core. If every file had been older, the gate would have built none of its own code and still passed, and the host's source-hash check doesn't catch a partly stale build. Fixes: (1) gate-host takes its lane first, then adds the worktree, running tools/slot as read from the tip with git show, and judges cleanup by what is left on disk. (2) xtask gate holds an flock on <target>/.vc-gate-lock for the whole run, taken before the first checkout, and hands each cargo a duplicate of the lock as stdin, so a killed gate keeps the lock until its build ends. (3) The working-tree gate builds in <target>/gate-tree, away from branch gates. If you gate on the Studio or share a CARGO_TARGET_DIR between gates, copy (1) and (2): tools/gate-host, and hold_target and cargo() in xtask/src/gate.rs. Next: Studio runs wait on one fixed lane while others sit idle (five queued on lane 1 at 03:25 with lane 3 empty). A first-free-lane fix is in progress.

data.summary: VectorCraft: Studio gate runs take the first free lane
data.body: Main e3d7a2a. xtask picked a lane from a hash of the checkout path, and the run waited on that one lane: five runs queued on lane 1 at 03:25, one for 51 minutes, while lane 3 sat empty. Now tools/gate-host tries the hashed lane first, then any free one. Each lane is held by a non-blocking flock on target/gate-host/lane<k>.lock, taken through perl because macOS has no flock command. When every lane is busy it retries all of them each second. A lane that a run from older code holds through its tools/slot slot is skipped after 5 s. A new caps-file line, `gate-lanes N` (1-16, default 4), sets the lane count; the shared caps file is unchanged. If your gate-host chooses lanes the same way, copy hold_lane and reap from tools/gate-host and the gate-lanes line in read_caps. tools/slot itself is unchanged.

data.summary: VectorCraft: decisions.md merge driver now merges row by row
data.body: Main a91a674. Queue 14 lost all six of its branches because one branch edited a row of docs/decisions.md that the others had only added rows above, and the add-only driver refused the merge. tools/merge-decisions now has a per-row three-way pass between git merge-file and the old add-only rule. It matches each table row across base, ours and theirs, takes one side's change or removal of a row the other side kept, and keeps both sides' new rows (ours, then theirs, at the top of the table; a row added word for word by both is kept once). A row both sides changed or removed, even the same way, still falls back to git's conflict: five Codex reviews in a row each built a case where pairing such rows went wrong. Text outside the tables must be unchanged on one side, and without python3 the pass is skipped. To copy it: tools/merge-decisions, the `docs/decisions.md merge=decisions` line in .gitattributes, and `git config merge.decisions.driver 'tools/merge-decisions %O %A %B %L %P'` once per clone.

data.summary: VectorCraft: land queues no longer stop on an xtask change, and reuse a review across a clean rebase
data.body: Main a7a4e00. Three changes to `land`, all to cut rebases and re-reviews. (1) When a landing changes xtask, `land --queue` hands the rest of the queue to an xtask built from the new main instead of stopping with 'check the xtask'. (2) A rebase whose commits keep the same patch ids reuses the branch's review: `patch_list` and `patch_reuse` in the review hook, records under branchpatch/, and `--rebased-from`; five new .githooks/test.sh cases cover it. (3) `land --queue` rebases each branch in a detached scratch worktree and moves the branch ref with an old-value check, so a land worktree no longer holds the branch an agent is working on. Each move is journalled, the worktree is looked up again at move and put-back, and a read-tree that fails after changing files keeps the ref and its record (also in fast_forward). If your land has the same rollback, check your fast_forward for that last case.

data.summary: VectorCraft: gate-host lane flake fixed; your tools/gate-host copies need the same two changes
data.body: Main cb104d2. The Studio lane tests (gate_host a_lane_an_older_run_holds_by_its_slot_is_passed_over and its two siblings) failed every gate run on the Studio: 0/20 before, 20/20 after. Two causes, both in tools/gate-host, so your copies likely have them. (1) A detached run inherited its caller's ARCADE_SLOT_HELD, so a gate inside a gate believed it already held lane 1. The detached run now unsets it. (2) The lane holder gave up on a lane after 5 s when tools/slot answered slowly, and passed over a free lane. It now waits for tools/slot's answer, which it recognises by the line 'slot: waiting for a <kind> slot', so keep that line word for word in your tools/slot. We also made the test hosts' orphan and reattach times long enough that load cannot run them out, and fixed two gate.rs test races (the zombie in scratch_sweeps_dead_gates_only, and a child that polled forever for a go file). Lesson: our first before-count said 20/20 because the test filter named the wrong module and ran zero tests; count each run's result line, not the exit code.

data.summary: VectorCraft: verify.rs and trace.rs split per game, so game branches stop conflicting there
data.body: Main 99d36f8. Our hottest conflict file was xtask/src/verify.rs: every game branch appended a Mechanic entry at the same spot, and every rebase conflicted. It is now verify/mod.rs (shared code), verify/games.rs (a registry of games, merged with git's union driver) and verify/games/<game>.rs; crates/core/src/trace.rs likewise became trace/<game>.rs. We proved the move changed nothing: verify --sensitivity printed the same 4,693 lines, all 168 replays traced byte-identical, and --dump-fed wrote the same records, checked after each game's move. tools/verify-moved finds where an old item went (--all <ref> checks every item). Two lessons: rebuild a long-lived move like this by rerunning its scripts on the new main rather than rebasing it (the scripts would have silently dropped main's new code in three places, so diff what they keep); and rustfmt's reorder_modules sorts mod lines, so a union-merged mod list can come out unsorted and fail a format check.

data.summary: VectorCraft: gate scratch names and gate-host nonces collided within one microsecond; check your copies
data.body: Main c998096. Two land tests failed a gate with 'index.lock: File exists' because both made the scratch worktree vc-gate-64660-499702000. The name was pid plus SystemTime subsec_nanos, and on macOS SystemTime only has microsecond resolution, so two scratches in one process in the same microsecond (parallel tests do this) shared a path; git worktree add accepts an existing empty directory, so nothing refused it. Fix (da48a5f): claim_dir builds vc-gate-<pid>-<nanos:09><count:06> from a process-wide atomic counter and claims the directory with fs::create_dir first (mkdir refuses a taken path; on EEXIST it tries the next count, up to 64; other errors fail), then fills it; fill_or_drop removes it if git fails. The gate-host run nonce had the same flaw (pid plus clock), and tools/gate-host treats a repeat nonce with the same args as the same run, so a second gate could have followed the first one's log and result; it is now nonce_of(pid, nanos, seq) (26a4979). If your xtask carries gate_scratch.rs or gate_host.rs, copy claim_dir, fill_or_drop, nonce_of, the SEQ counters and the two fake-clock tests. No change to tools/slot, tools/gate-host or .githooks. Lesson: grep for names built from the clock alone (subsec_nanos, as_nanos, date +%N).
